title: Approved bounded argv process.spawn
objective: Expose the first public process.spawn capability as an argv-only, locally approved, workspace-bound, zero-network execution path backed by the already-qualified AppContainer and Job Object executor, while preserving bounded output, verified termination, secret isolation, and a hard separation from PowerShell and shell command strings.

include: typed MCP process.spawn tool with executable plus argv array
positive Windows executable policy restricted to the exact qualified System32 whoami.exe target
sanitized inherited environment with no caller-provided environment overrides
local approval bound to the exact normalized execution plan
AppContainer suspended launch and token verification
Job assignment and membership before resume
bounded stdout/stderr and typed termination failures
verified zero active Job processes before timeout/output-limit results
exclude: cmd.exe or shell interpolation as an API primitive
direct PowerShell executable authority through process.spawn

authority_delta.filesystem: No new filesystem capability; execution cwd must resolve within the already trusted workspace
authority_delta.process: Adds one approved public argv-only process.spawn capability, positively restricted on Windows to the exact qualified System32 whoami.exe target, routed through the contained Windows executor
authority_delta.network: None; network_class must be NONE and AppContainer receives zero capabilities
authority_delta.ui_input: None; only the existing independent local approval surface is used
authority_delta.secrets: No new secret access; caller environment overrides are absent and Cotra/tunnel secrets remain excluded
authority_delta.approval: Every process.spawn execution requires a fresh local approval bound to the exact normalized plan

invariants: The MCP interface accepts executable and argv separately and never a shell command string
PowerShell remains a separate denied capability
Windows public executable authority is a positive allowlist restricted to the exact qualified System32 whoami.exe target in this grain
The executable must resolve to an existing absolute file
The cwd must resolve inside the selected trusted workspace
Caller-provided environment variables are not accepted in this grain
The child inherits only the existing sanitized environment allowlist and explicit standard handles
The AppContainer has zero network capabilities
The child is created suspended and verified as AppContainer before resume
The child is assigned to the kill-on-close Job and membership is verified before resume
Timeout or output-limit classification is returned only after verified Job quiescence
Failure to prove termination returns TerminationUnverified
Approval is bound to executable, argv, cwd, limits, stdin policy, network class, workspace, and policy revision
No background execution or approval reuse is introduced
Generic descendant-producing executable authority cannot widen until post-primary-exit drain/lifecycle hardening is separately qualified

acceptance.claim: Policy authorizes only process.spawn/spawn with a valid bounded argv request, positively restricts the Windows executable to the exact qualified fixture, and continues denying PowerShell and unknown process operations.
The MCP edge exposes a typed process.spawn tool with executable, argv, cwd, timeout/output bounds, null stdin policy, and network_class=NONE; it exposes no raw command-string field.
cotrad normalizes the request, constructs a sanitized ExecutionPlan, obtains fresh local approval bound to the exact plan digest, and does not execute when approval is denied or unavailable.

Native Windows exact-head tests execute the approved System32 whoami.exe argv fixture through the public daemon/provider path and return bounded stdout/stderr plus exit code with AppContainer identity, pre-resume Job membership, and zero active Job processes verified.
Native Windows timeout/stdout-limit/stderr-limit regressions retain typed ProcessTimeout/OutputLimit/TerminationUnverified semantics and SG-000009/SG-000009A qualification remains green.

Tests prove cwd escape, relative/missing or non-allowlisted executable authority, shell/PowerShell targets, NUL argv, non-NONE network class, non-null stdin policy, caller env injection, and over-limit requests fail closed before execution.
Exact-head Windows/Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine Jev, and Alibaba Open Code Review gates pass with zero unresolved blocking findings.

done_when: The approved argv-only process.spawn path is merged with exact-head and post-merge verification, public PowerShell/network/background authority remains absent, and governance records the evidence without widening executable authority.
